case: declaring an unanswered finding unpinnable, with a reason
why: The benign twin of r19-pin-citing-a-review-finding-deleted, moving the same control in the other direction. F6A-01 is one of the 37 findings this package declares a source for and says nothing about; adding an `unpinnable` row with a reason takes that set to 36, under the ceiling of 37. This must PASS: the ceiling exists to refuse a pin deletion, not to freeze the pin file, and the legitimate way to stop answering a finding -- say so, in writing, in the table a reviewer reads -- has to remain cheaper than the illegitimate one. A checker that refused this would be refusing every future declaration, which would teach an author to delete the finding_sources row instead and leave nothing behind at all. The `unpinnable` row alone is now HALF the edit: F6R-01's partition check reports 'declared but not unanswered' for a finding that is both unpinnable and in `not_answered`, so the benign edit this fixture models has to leave the partition consistent -- which is the partition doing its job on a fixture rather than on a repair. DRIFT REPAIR by lane r7-contracts-c: this benign fixture was FALSELY EXCLUDED on the merged head. It is the same class the package names elsewhere -- a fixture that encodes a snapshot of a table another lane then grew. The patch is regenerated from the current tree and the old shape is recorded here, because a benign fixture that fails looks exactly like a repair that broke something. REGENERATED 2026-09-15 (lane r8-contracts-f). The `replace` above carried a FROZEN snapshot of `#/not_answered`, taken when the table held 36 rows, and this lane grew it by the eleven F6AA rows and shrank it by three crossings. The partition check refused the benign case with the F6AA ids 'in neither half' -- a benign fixture failing reads exactly like a repair that broke something, which is why the class is recorded here rather than silently rewritten. The map is now derived from the committed table minus the single key this fixture means to trim, so it is the same mutation over the current tree. It will freeze again the next time the table grows; the durable cure is a patch op that removes one key rather than replacing the map, which the applier does not have.
